defect.summary: narrow-T's A5 AMI-ceiling guard, which exists to stop a benign phase change from reading as drift, cannot fire above two event classes, and the bridge writes seven. A healthy agent reads as drift, goes to ALARM and is held. The hold cannot clear, because a held agent stops writing. Expected fix: the guard reasons over the class SET of the window, not a two-class assumption. The post-27th shape ('clean acts, then all held acts') must read as a phase change, not drift.

arbiter.word: I open the core for this one defect, narrow-T's guard, because a healthy agent must not be held forever. Fix the smallest honest thing, freeze what you learn, and close the door on the 29th.

conditions: The existing 20 frozen scenarios stay byte-identical. They live in src/mica/verdict-logic.frozen.json (tested by verdict-logic.test.ts). This ticket does NOT open that file, so the door keeps it pinned.

AMENDED 2026-09-22 by Frank: of the 38 existing projections, exactly ONE may move — t/drifted-alarm, from ALARM to CANNOT_ASSESS, because it froze the defect as correct. The other 37 stay byte-identical. TWO new projections are added: the 21st (the post-27th phase change reading CANNOT_ASSESS) and a 22nd, a genuine partial drift in the live vocabulary that MUST read ALARM — the proof the repair did not switch the reader off. If any other projection moves, revert, do not re-freeze.
The commit that ships the repair also re-pins every file it changed (npm run core-door -- --propose-repin T1-narrow-t-guard). One change per relay.
